53: Energy consumed per second when active cooling is running at full strength (because your ship's temperature is approaching the overheating threshold).
54: Interference with your ship's cooling abilities. Its cooling systems will only be about 75% effective at a cooling inefficiency of 5, and 30% at an inefficiency of 10.
55: Protection provided against corrosion damage. Increases by the given factor how much corrosion damage a ship can withstand before it loses as much hull as an unprotected ship.
57: Energy consumed per second when resisting corrosion damage.
58: Fuel consumed per second when resisting corrosion damage.
59: Heat generated per second when resisting corrosion damage.
60: Cost, in credits. If you have sold any used (depreciated) items today, you can buy them back for the same price you sold them for.
61: How much this ship costs toward your fleet capacity. Your flagship and parked escorts do not count toward the capacity. You may exceed your capacity while landed, but will not be able to depart if you go over your capacity.
62: Protection provided against shield discharge damage. Increases by the given factor how much discharge damage a ship can withstand before it loses as much shielding as an unprotected ship.
63: How much shield discharge damage this ship can resist per second.
64: Energy consumed per second when resisting discharge damage.
65: Fuel consumed per second when resisting discharge damage.
66: Heat generated per second when resisting discharge damage.
67: Protection provided against shield disruption damage. Increases by the given factor how much disruption damage a ship can withstand before its shields are as disrupted as those of an unprotected ship.
68: Shield disruption damage resisted per second.
69: Energy consumed per second when resisting disruption damage.
70: Fuel consumed per second when resisting disruption damage.
71: Heat generated per second when resisting disruption damage.
72: Limits the maximum speed of a ship.
73: Reduces drag. Increases the top speed of a ship by the given factor.
74: The number of ships from the "Drone" category that this ship can carry.
75: The amount of energy this outfit adds to your ship's energy capacity. This allows you to temporarily use more power than your generators produce.
76: Energy consumed per second while in flight.
77: Energy generated per second. If your ship has weapons other than beam weapons, you will probably also need batteries to store energy in.
78: Tons of engine space this outfit takes up.
